steps.explanationAfterStep: This is a Mannich reaction with indole as the enol-like nucleophile. Attack at C-3 lets the nitrogen take the positive charge directly while the benzene ring stays aromatic. Stopping with the charge on the ring carbon next to nitrogen is also accepted: it is another drawing of the same cation.
Losing the proton restores the aromatic indole. Gramine is a useful intermediate: the dimethylamino group can later leave (after methylation), so C-3 can be given other carbon groups.

title: Gramine synthesis
subtitle: A Mannich reaction of indole: the iminium ion is attacked from C-3
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 29

reactants.caption: indole + the dimethyliminium ion (from formaldehyde and dimethylamine) + acetate
hintTiers: Indole is an enamine fused to a benzene ring. Which carbon of the five-membered ring is the enamine's nucleophilic carbon?

The C=C π bond of the five-membered ring attacks the CH₂ carbon of the iminium ion from the carbon further from nitrogen; the C=N⁺ π bond moves onto the dimethylamino nitrogen; the indole nitrogen lone pair forms a C=N π bond. Three arrows.

The ring C=C π bond → a new bond from the carbon with the drawn H to the iminium CH₂; the iminium C=N π bond → a lone pair on its nitrogen; the indole nitrogen lone pair → a π bond to the carbon next to it.
reactants.learnerPrompt: Indole attacks the iminium ion. Draw it, and put the positive charge on the indole nitrogen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Attack at C-2 gives a cation that nitrogen can stabilise only by breaking up the benzene ring's sextet. Attack at C-3 puts the charge straight onto nitrogen and leaves the benzene ring untouched: indole reacts at C-3.
The indole nitrogen lone pair is part of the aromatic system, so the nitrogen is not nucleophilic under these mildly acidic conditions. Indole reacts at carbon.
Acetate can add to the iminium ion, but that adduct just falls apart again. Indole is the nucleophile that leads somewhere.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right carbon of indole. The CH₂ carbon now has five bonds: move the C=N⁺ π bond onto its nitrogen.

indoleninium-ion.caption: the 3H-indolium ion + acetate
hintTiers: Which carbon of the five-membered ring is sp³, and which of its hydrogens can leave?
Acetate takes the H on the sp³ carbon; the C–H electrons form a C=C π bond; the C=N⁺ π bond moves back onto nitrogen. Three arrows.
Acetate O⁻ lone pair → a new O–H bond to the ring H; that C–H bond → the π bond to the next ring carbon; the C=N π bond → a lone pair on the indole nitrogen.
indoleninium-ion.learnerPrompt: Acetate removes a proton and the five-membered ring becomes aromatic again.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The dimethylamino group is a base, and it may well shuttle the proton, but acetate is drawn here to do the job. Use acetate.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right proton. The C–H electrons now form the ring C=C bond, and the C=N π bond returns to nitrogen.

mechanismSummary: Formaldehyde and dimethylamine in acetic acid give the dimethyliminium ion (as in any Mannich reaction). Indole attacks it from C-3: the nitrogen lone pair pushes, the charge ends on nitrogen, and the benzene ring is never disturbed. Attack at C-2 would need the benzene ring's electrons to stabilise the cation, so it is much slower. Acetate removes the proton from C-3 and the ring becomes aromatic again: gramine.
